EL2-F-01.hint: Start from the basic graph \(y=b^{x}\), which has the \(x\)-axis as its asymptote. A vertical shift moves the asymptote with it; a reflection over the \(x\)-axis flips which side the graph is on.
slips: Reading the asymptote from the horizontal shift. Only the number added or subtracted outside the exponential moves it.
Giving the range as \((k,\infty)\) after a reflection over the \(x\)-axis. The graph is then below \(y=k\).

EL2-A-01.hint: Read the transformations in order: the number inside the exponent shifts left or right, a minus sign out front reflects, and the number added at the end shifts up or down.
slips: Shifting the wrong way horizontally. \(x-2\) in the exponent shifts right.
Evaluating at \(x=0\) incorrectly. Substitute into the whole expression, including the shift.

parts.q: State the domain in interval notation.
parts.a: \((-\infty, \infty)\). An exponential function can be evaluated at any real input.

parts.q: State the range in interval notation.
parts.a: \((5, \infty)\). The graph of \(5^{x}\) stays above \(y = 0\). Shifting up \(5\) units moves that boundary to \(y = 5\).

parts.q: Give the equation of the horizontal asymptote.
parts.a: \(y = 5\). A horizontal shift does not move a horizontal asymptote.
